draft.title: Customers, suppliers and competitors
card: The market (operating) environment is made up of the groups a business deals with directly. They are its customers, suppliers and competitors. A business can influence them, but it cannot control them.
the people who buy the product. Their tastes and willingness to pay decide what sells, so a business must keep finding out what they want.
the businesses that provide inputs such as stock, materials and services. They affect the price, quality and reliability of what a business receives, and so its own costs and product quality.
other businesses that sell similar products to the same customers. They push a business to improve its quality and service or to lower its prices, or customers may switch.
draft.remember: Customers decide what sells, suppliers shape costs and quality, and competitors push a business to do better.

a.q: Which group in the market environment decides what products actually sell?
a.why: Customers choose whether to buy, so their tastes and willingness to pay decide what sells. Competitors affect what customers can choose between, but they do not make the purchase decision.

b.q: Priya owns a bakery in Orange. A new bakery opens across the street and sells similar bread at lower prices. Which influence is this, and what is a likely response?
opts: Competitors, so she may lower prices or improve quality
Competitors, so she should change her flour prices
Suppliers, so she may lower prices or improve quality
Customers, so she should ask the new bakery to raise prices
b.why: The new bakery sells to the same customers, so it is a competitor. Competitors push a business to lower prices or improve quality. A supplier provides inputs and does not sell to Priya's customers, and she cannot control what the rival charges.
b.clue: Who is selling to the same customers as Priya?

b.best: Competitors, so she may lower prices or improve quality
